title: Chapter 88 — Campaigns, Events & The Retail Calendar
intro: The promo calendar mastered, the event playbook, and quiet-season craft.

sections.title: The Seasonal Rhythm
sections.content:
January-February: post-holiday slowdown. Hit your builder pipeline. Follow up on every open quote from the holidays. March-April: spring renovation kicks off. Kitchen packages. Tax refund money arrives.

May — Victoria Day and Memorial Day: major promotional weekend, one of the top three selling weekends. Pre-sell the week before. June-July: outdoor living season. Condo move-in season.

August-September: laundry picks up. Labour Day is another top promo weekend. October: renovation completion push — urgency is real. November — Black Friday: biggest single sales period, compressed margins. December: year-end builder close-outs.

The best reps plan 30 days ahead. They know what is coming and they ride the wave instead of being surprised by it.

sections.title: Event Selling
sections.content:
VIP shopping events, cooking demos, designer evenings — these are pipeline accelerators. An invite-only event makes customers feel special. In-person demos convert better than any ad.

The event playbook: curate the guest list from your CRM. Send personal invitations. Offer event-only pricing or exclusive previews. Have your design consultant available. Follow up with everyone who attended within 48 hours.

sections.title: Quiet Season Craft
sections.content:
The slow months are not down time. They are building time. This is when you train on new products, prospect new builder accounts, clean your CRM, attend manufacturer trainings, and build the pipeline that will pay you during peak season.

Every rep who coasts in January and February scrambles in May. Every rep who prospects in January has a full pipeline when the promotions hit.
